claim: You can show your published Capell pages on a separate website or mobile app, such as one built with Next.js or Nuxt.
Your editors keep working in Capell as they do now; the package adds no admin screen.
Your developer can ask for one page by its address, list pages by type, search page titles or fetch a directory of pages.
Lists arrive twenty at a time by default, up to a hundred, and each list points to the next batch if there is one.
Pages that are live today are the only ones returned.
Their content is cleaned of anything unsafe on the way out.
Drafts stay private unless your developer uses a personal key made for previewing.
Sending starts once your developer has added the front end's address and a secret, and the messages go out as background jobs, which your developer or host keeps running.
When an editor publishes, saves or deletes a page, or a page's dates pass, Capell can send your front end a signed message. Each message names the site and page that changed.
